To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed a recombinant strain of E.coli to display fucosylation, which is a key feature of the Lewis blood group antigen.
We have designed a recombinant strain of E.coli that displays the Lewis Y structure on the cell surface.
we designed a recombinant strain of E.coli to express the ganglioside GM3 on the cell surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel platform for the synthesis of fucosylated oligosaccharides in E.coli.
the design of recombinant bacteria for glycomimicry, i.e. the production of bacterial glycolipids that resemble human cell-surface carbohydrates.
the development of glycomimicry, a strategy that aims at displaying glycoconjugate structures on the cell surface of bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the glycomimicry strategy is a powerful tool for displaying complex oligosaccharide structures on the surface of bacteria, and the results obtained in this study are a proof of concept for the feasibility of the glycomimics strategy. [1]
we have developed the first glycomimetic display system in E.coli, which allows the display of a fucosylated glycolipid on the bacterial surface.
the fucosylated lipo-oligoglycans of recombinant E. coli are glycomimicry structures that mimic gangliosides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the display of the fucosylated gangliomannose antigen GM3 on the surface of E.coli K12 is achieved by the action of 5 glycosyltransferase enzymes.
the lipo- and oligosaccharide of E.coli K12 is an excellent scaffold to assemble a large number of complex glycan structures.
we have developed an E.coli strain that displays the Lewis Y antigen on the outer membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to display fucose-containing motifs on the cell surface of E.coli.

the use of a truncated lipid A scaffold is a promising approach for the display of complex oligosaccharides on bacterial surfaces, as it allows the display of a wide range of complex glycans on bacterial surfaces.
glycosylation of a recombinant LPS can be achieved by a combination of heterologous enzymes, which are not necessarily of a homologous nature.
